candidates.label: A1 (A trimmed, B=base)
candidates.change: A startup 56 -> 49 turns, same first-anchor address, same capture code: band math in 16 bit (xor dx,dx; mov ax,si; mov cx,3C00h; div cx; lea ax,[si+2CA2h]; sub ax,dx; checked equal to the old 8-bit result for all 65536 load addresses); dead mov dx,[4A17h]/and dx,0/or dx,0FFBh -> mov dx,0FFBh; jmp to the next line removed; mov sp,di/add sp,100h -> lea sp,[di+100h]; dead zombie_entry/zombie_scan removed; the 18th template byte (89h, first byte of old zombie_entry) kept as db so the rebuilt worker bytes are identical. The first 9 instructions (the [4A17h]->[9769h] hook copy and the INT 87h zom20a capture) are unchanged and keep their timing.

candidates.label: A1+B2 (both trimmed)
candidates.change: A1 plus the same trims in B: 16-bit band math on B's main path (lea ax,[si+10A2h]), dead mov dx,[4A17h]/and/or -> mov dx,0FFBh, lea sp,[di+600h]. B main path is 6 turns shorter, captured-zombie path 3 turns shorter; zombie_entry logic unchanged.

candidates.label: B2 only (A=base)
candidates.change: B trimmed as in A1+B2; A is the base.
candidates.groupNotes: 2025 +0.00178; strong +0.00635; threat +0.02101 [0.003,0.039]; multi -0.04444 [-0.066,-0.023] (V6x3 -0.056, mix -0.033). Most of the multi-copy loss comes from the B trim.

threatFindings.threat: Several copies of V6-family clones (V6 x3, V6Guard x3) punish a faster startup
threatFindings.evidence: Threat job 20261003183134999-A001-threat-038rf (copies 3, 10 cohorts each, 900 battles/arm), candidate A1+B2 minus base: lead_V6 -0.0523 [-0.0797,-0.0249] W/L 2/8, lead_V6Guard -0.0282 [-0.0552,-0.0013] W/L 2/8, lead_V4 +0.0229. Screen multi group was negative for A1+B2 (-0.060) and B2 alone (-0.044), less so for A1 alone (-0.011).
threatFindings.impact: The timing trim is not free: against crowds of identical-lattice clones (same bands and phases as ours), starting earlier loses. Mechanism not traced. Hypothesis: when a clone shares our band, the later writer owns the shared anchor, so arriving first is now a disadvantage.

threatFindings.threat: Startup-time savings help against the 2025 field
threatFindings.evidence: A1 screen 2025 group +0.0169 [0.0067,0.0270] W/L 12/2 (only CI that excludes 0 for A1). A1+B2 2025 +0.0127 is not significant. Needs a fresh-field check.

recommendation: Do not promote any of the three as they stand. A1+B2 has the largest ALL gain (+0.0145), but the multi-copy V6/V6Guard loss is confirmed (-0.05 / -0.03), so it fails the 'multi not worse than -0.01' gate. A1 (A-only trim, +0.0055, 2025 +0.017) falls just short of the +0.006 bar; its multi loss is small (-0.011), so it could go through confirmation as an optional near-threshold candidate. Next experiment: an A1 variant that keeps the old startup length (for example a dwell/padding before call far) only when a same-band clone is likely, or a trace of A1+B2 vs V6x3, to find out why arriving first loses to clones.
notes: Engine check: AAM/AAD are not implemented in the v6 engine (throw), so I used 16-bit DIV instead. LEA r16,[mem] and 16-bit DIV are supported. Build outputs are in agent2/night/scratch/A001/build. B2 was generated by agent2/night/scratch/A001/mkB2.cjs.
